utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, can you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is the Case Number IT-97-24-A, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to call the appearances for the parties. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Appearing for the Prosecution, Mark McKeon, with our case manager Susan Grogan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McKeon. And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is John Ostojic and I am here on behalf of Dr. Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Stakic, can you hear me and understand what I am saying? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I can hear you and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Can you repeat it.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I can hear you and understand you in my own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [In English] May I sit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Yes, please. This is a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires that a Status Conference be convened within 120 days of the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation to thereto, including the mental and physical condition of the person. Our last Status Conference in this case was on September 2, 2004. I would like now to ask Mr. Stakic whether you have any issues to raise in relation to your detention and whether you would like to express any concerns regarding your mental or physical well-being. Mr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I must say that since late November or early December I have had high blood pressure. This did happen earlier, but it was always somewhere about 150/90 with occasional headaches, which I paid no heed to. Being a doctor myself, I thought that was on account of the climate or the weather changing or difficulty with my sinuses. However, now the pressure was 165/115. I thought my head was about to burst. Eventually I got a prescription from the doctor. I was taking medicines for a while. It would go down and then rise to 160/60 after a couple of days. I have received some lab results in the meantime which seem to be fine. I have been diagnosed with a post-stress reaction. I'm receiving therapy three times a day over a time period of six months; we shall be monitoring the results and see what happens. Occasionally I've had the same high pressure, 150/90, 150/95, but I don't think that this should cause any further problems. As for the medical staff and other staff at the Detention Unit, I have no complaints whatsoever. They have been most helpful and I have received all the assistance required. My lab results have been processed and treatment has been administered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stakic. I am pleased to hear that despite the problems that you had in the context of your blood pressure, that you have received good medical treatment which is continuing. And I do hope that the problem will get better and better. I take it that there is nothing else that you would like to tell me today? In which case, you may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have been on therapy. I would just like to say that we're treating the symptoms here, not the cause, unfortunately. Other than that, I have nothing to say. Thank you. Thank you for your kind words, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stakic. Do sit down. At the moment the parties' submissions on the respective appeals on the trial judgement are complete. I am not in a position today to inform you precisely when the Appeals Chamber's hearing on this appeal will be scheduled, but we will be aiming for it to occur sometime in June, if we can. Does either of the parties wish to raise any issues at this time in Mr. McKeon?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCKEON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. There's nothing we wish to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: None at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If there are no other issues, I thank the parties for their attendance and all the proceedings to a close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: adjourned at 12.36 p.m.
